note: Tool names, descriptions and schemas are REA's own (MIT, github.com/morluto/rea).

tools.name: inspect_analysis_settings
tools.title: Inspect Analysis Settings
tools.description: Inspect REA's editable runtime admission sizes, deadlines and worker heaps, their bounds, launch values and application points. No active target is required. Filters intersect. If an error already names a setting and its bounds, update_analysis_settings can be called directly. Explicit per-call arguments override runtime defaults. Active worker values are not observed by this configuration view.

tools.name: update_analysis_settings
tools.title: Update Analysis Settings
tools.description: When REA names an adjustable limit, atomically set or reset its runtime default, then retry once work and cleanup have settled. No inspection call is required when the error supplies the bounds. Changes apply only to new work, survive target close/open, and disappear on REA restart. Reset restores launch configuration. Does not edit files, restart providers, raise host limits, or override explicit per-call arguments.

tools.name: inspect_desktop_application
tools.title: Inspect Desktop Application
tools.description: Inspect a local desktop application directory using bounded listings, file headers and selected metadata. Returns .NET, Unity Mono/IL2CPP, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker and Electron candidates, supporting paths/range hashes, component path markers and concrete next probes. No target execution, extraction, network or target changes. Default summary retains complete Evidence for inspect_analysis_view kind desktop-application; collections files/candidates/components/next_probes support paging and field selection, with exact file paths or candidate families. detail complete returns every retained fact inline. Snapshot identity covers examined metadata/read ranges, not all file contents; coverage and unavailable probes remain explicit.

path.description: Local filesystem path used by this operation.

max_entries.description: Maximum permitted entries for this operation.

max_probe_bytes.description: Maximum permitted probe bytes for this operation.

inputSchema.description: Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

tools.name: inspect_model_artifact
tools.title: Inspect Model Artifact
tools.description: Inspect local GGUF v2/v3 or safetensors declarations by content, without loading models or executing code. Default hash header reads only the header: full-file SHA-256 and Evidence subject are unknown; artifact.header_sha256 is a scoped prefix commitment, not weight identity. hash full additionally streams all file bytes for SHA-256. Optional view returns a selected metadata/tensor/type page plus model context in this call. Summary retains complete Evidence for inspect_analysis_view kind model-artifact, collection metadata (keys/indices/fields) or tensors (names/types/indices/fields), with stable header-scoped indices and paging. Metadata arrays retain eight-element typed previews; scalar metadata is complete. Tensor counts, shapes, numeric type IDs and offsets are observed; textual types and parameter/storage totals use established format facts. Unknown or historically ambiguous GGUF types retain IDs with unknown nonempty byte lengths; ambiguous identities use AMBIGUOUS_<id> labels. Unresolved Q8_1 and K-block layouts also keep nonempty byte lengths unknown. Tensor payload, model behavior and inference quality are not inspected. One active inspection, 100 MB header ceiling and 32 MiB retained-facts budget; resource refusals are explicit. No network, external files, Python, model runtime, extraction or deserialization of pickle.

path.description: Local filesystem path used by this operation.

hash.description: header reads declarations only; full streams all bytes for SHA-256

view.description: Return this selected page with compact model context, retaining complete Evidence; requires summary detail

tools.name: inspect_gpu_code_objects
tools.title: Inspect Gpu Code Objects
tools.description: Inspect static CUDA/HIP GPU code objects in local ELF/PE hosts, CUDA fatbins, CUBIN, PTX and Clang HIP bundles (CUDA LZ4/Zstd and CCOB v1/v2/v3 zlib/Zstd). Default inventory reads directories; full-file SHA-256 always streams every byte. analysis kernels decodes only selected object_ids/targets (object_ids require expected_sha256 from their inventory), retaining all inventory rows and explicit partial/unknown states. Reports PTX virtual registers, CUBIN physical registers/nv.info parameters/shared memory and AMDGPU MessagePack kernel declarations separately. No GPU tools, target execution, network, SASS disassembly or host launch correlation. Unsupported CUDA compression retains encoded locations. Default summary retains complete Evidence; optional view returns a selected targets/objects/kernels page or PTX text page in this call. inspect_analysis_view kind gpu-code-objects reuses retained facts without reopening files; PTX text uses UTF-16 code-unit pages. Object IDs are positional within artifact.sha256. One active inspection; 128 MiB/object, 512 MiB decoded work, 16 MiB retained facts. Full Evidence includes selected PTX text artifacts with SHA-256 and encoded/decoded provenance.

path.description: Local filesystem path used by this operation.

expected_sha256.description: Require the current full-file digest; mandatory when selecting inventory object_ids

object_ids.description: Decode only these inventory IDs; IDs are scoped to the artifact SHA-256

targets.description: Decode only exact target declarations, preserving all inventory rows

tools.name: annotate_native_function
tools.title: Annotate Native Function
tools.description: Atomically update one function name and/or entry comments, read them back, and return a refreshed complete function dossier. Ghidra changes its ephemeral session analysis database only; original executable bytes remain unchanged. Empty comment text clears that comment. Edits remain available to subsequent MCP calls until close; CLI returns the updated dossier before discarding its session. Invalid edits roll back the entire operation. Windows P0 and providers without this capability are unsupported.

tools.name: inspect_native_load_image
tools.title: Inspect Native Load Image
tools.description: Verify the provider's loaded DOS MZ or explicitly selected COM image against its immutable target snapshot: complete original/modified source-byte digests, header/module file mappings and memory digests, relocations and external entry. Returns measured observations and independent checks with mismatch coordinates. COM verification includes its imposed entry register context and does not claim PSP/runtime coverage. Overlay and uninitialized coverage remain explicit; other formats return unsupported. Does not execute or modify the target.

tools.name: inspect_native_data_type
tools.title: Inspect Native Data Type
tools.description: Inspect one recovered type by exact database category path or defined typed data address. Returns observed size, alignment, packing, fields, bitfields, enum values, and child type identities; source-level authority and flexible-tail semantics remain unknown unless substantiated.

tools.name: inspect_native_instruction
tools.title: Inspect Native Instruction
tools.description: Inspect one exact code or data address: decoded bytes, mnemonic, ordered operand tokens, flow, outgoing instruction references and typed incoming references where available. Incoming references preserve source, access kind, operand index and analysis provenance even at data addresses; they do not prove runtime access. Memory addressing decomposition is unavailable when the provider supplies only tokens. Data, interior instruction addresses and undecodable bytes are distinct outcomes.

tools.name: resolve_native_call_targets
tools.title: Resolve Native Call Targets
tools.description: Resolve one explicit static call site using typed provider call references. Preserves ambiguous targets as candidates and unresolved computed calls as unknown; does not execute code or traverse a call graph.

tools.name: address_name
tools.title: Address Name
tools.description: Resolve the primary analyzed name at a code or data address. Headless providers require an explicit address; GUI providers may default to their current cursor. Null means the provider has no primary name at that address.

tools.name: comment
tools.title: Comment
tools.description: Read the regular analysis comment at an address, defaulting to the current cursor. This is read-only and returns null when no comment exists; use set_comment to persist a finding.

tools.name: current_address
tools.title: Current Address
tools.description: Return Hopper's current cursor address for the selected document. Use only for interactive navigation state; prefer explicit addresses in reproducible investigations.

tools.name: current_procedure
tools.title: Current Procedure
tools.description: Return the analyzed procedure containing Hopper's current cursor. This uses GUI cursor state and is not a procedure-name lookup.

tools.name: current_document
tools.title: Current Document
tools.description: Return the document currently selected by REA's Hopper bridge.

tools.name: goto_address
tools.title: Goto Address
tools.description: Move Hopper's GUI cursor to a mapped address and return the observed cursor address. Interior coordinates snap to the containing analyzed object's start. Unmapped destinations fail without moving the cursor. This changes navigation state but not analysis data; use explicit-address tools for headless workflows.

tools.name: inline_comment
tools.title: Inline Comment
tools.description: Read the inline instruction comment at an address, defaulting to the current cursor. Returns null when absent; use set_inline_comment to write one.

tools.name: list_bookmarks
tools.title: List Bookmarks
tools.description: List every bookmark in the selected Hopper document as address and name pairs; unnamed bookmarks retain a null name. Use bookmarks as analyst-authored navigation aids; this does not discover code references.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.title: List Documents
tools.description: List provider program or document identities. Hopper may expose several documents; a Ghidra headless session contains exactly its one imported Program.

tools.name: list_names
tools.title: List Names
tools.description: List every analyzed memory and external symbol as address/value pairs. Provider metadata distinguishes Ghidra primary, dynamic, external, type, and source facts when available. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: list_procedures
tools.title: List Procedures
tools.description: List every analyzed procedure as address/value pairs after provider analysis. Ghidra metadata distinguishes thunks and external functions; use returned addresses in later function operations. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: list_segments
tools.title: List Segments
tools.description: List segments or memory blocks using exclusive end addresses. Ghidra reports block permissions, address space, image base, initialization, and overlay facts; Hopper marks unavailable permissions explicitly.

tools.name: list_strings
tools.title: List Strings
tools.description: List every provider-reported string object or candidate, or filter to one address, as address/value pairs with encoding, terminator status, and byte length when available. Hopper reads complete typed objects and retains its original display text as provider_value; long literals may span adjacent unterminated objects. Kuna scans mapped printable sequences of at least five characters, including unterminated fragments; references are not computed. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: next_address
tools.title: Next Address
tools.description: Return the next analyzed object address after an explicit address or current cursor. This is a navigation primitive, not instruction-flow or CFG analysis.

tools.name: prev_address
tools.title: Prev Address
tools.description: Return the previous analyzed object start before an explicit address or current cursor. This is a navigation primitive and may fail at document boundaries; data objects and instructions remain distinct from control flow.

tools.name: procedure_address
tools.title: Procedure Address
tools.description: Resolve an unambiguous procedure symbol name or provider-normalized address to its canonical entry address. External address spaces remain explicit.

tools.name: procedure_assembly
tools.title: Procedure Assembly
tools.description: Return assembly for one analyzed procedure identified by symbol or hexadecimal address. Use when pseudocode loses calling-convention or instruction-level detail; output is currently returned as one unpaginated string. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in Evidence limitations.

tools.name: procedure_callees
tools.title: Procedure Callees
tools.description: Return the provider's resolved direct callees for one procedure identified by symbol or address. Unresolved indirect calls may be absent; use analyze_function and typed references to preserve available edge uncertainty. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in Evidence limitations.

tools.name: procedure_callers
tools.title: Procedure Callers
tools.description: Return the provider's resolved direct callers for one procedure identified by symbol or address. Results reflect completed static analysis and may omit unresolved indirect references. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in Evidence limitations.

tools.name: procedure_info
tools.title: Procedure Info
tools.description: Return provider metadata for one procedure identified by symbol or address: entrypoint, signature, locals, size, block count, and complete inclusive body ranges when observed. Extents reflect the provider's analyzed body; Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut it are reported in Evidence limitations. Hopper locals preserve observed names and signed stack displacements; source types remain unknown. Body byte count and enclosing span remain distinct; unavailable extent is explicit.

tools.name: read_function_instructions
tools.title: Read Function Instructions
tools.description: Return every raw instruction for one analyzed procedure. Instruction text and body extent are provider-specific. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in limitations.

tools.name: search_bytes
tools.title: Search Bytes
tools.description: Find masked byte signatures in initialized analyzed memory. Hex byte pairs and ?? wildcards are supported; an optional equal-length hex mask selects bits. Bounds are inclusive. Matches are ordered by provider address and never span blocks. Coverage describes this page; reuse the same query with next_cursor to continue. Uninitialized blocks are listed separately. Ghidra only; Hopper is unavailable.

tools.name: read_bytes
tools.title: Read Bytes
tools.description: Read analyzed bytes from one provider-normalized virtual address. The hexadecimal payload reports the exact returned length; incomplete reads remain explicit and unsupported provider APIs return typed capability unavailability.

tools.name: address_to_file_offset
tools.title: Address To File Offset
tools.description: Map one provider-normalized virtual address to its original nonnegative file offset. Hopper verifies the original bytes against the selected executable digest and translates FAT image-relative offsets using the loaded header. Results preserve the provider coordinate, image base, and source path. Unmapped addresses fail explicitly; changed or unavailable sources return typed errors retaining native mapping facts as partial evidence.

tools.name: procedure_references
tools.title: Procedure References
tools.description: Return every raw incoming or outgoing reference edge for one procedure. Endpoint procedures are resolved only from provider containment. Ghidra preserves detailed reference flags. Hopper preserves native CallReference classifications and exact endpoints while leaving unavailable detailed flags explicit.

tools.name: procedure_pseudo_code
tools.title: Procedure Pseudo Code
tools.description: Decompile one analyzed procedure by symbol name or provider-normalized address. Ghidra also accepts file-offset:0x... selectors and falls back to a unique source-file mapping when a 0x-prefixed number resolves to no procedure; existing analysis addresses take precedence and ambiguous mappings fail explicitly. Returns provider-specific pseudocode, never original source or cross-provider text equivalence, and may return null; request procedure_assembly when instruction precision matters. Ghidra no-return assumptions may cut the analyzed body; Evidence limitations report observed terminal calls and available callee identities.

tools.name: resolve_containing_procedure
tools.title: Resolve Containing Procedure
tools.description: Resolve an arbitrary address, including an interior instruction or exact external entry, to its provider-analyzed containing procedure. A negative result distinguishes outside segments from not in a procedure and is never guessed from nearby symbols.

tools.name: search_procedures
tools.title: Search Procedures
tools.description: Search every analyzed procedure name using literal matching by default or regex when requested. Results are deterministic and complete. Hopper regex mode uses ECMAScript Unicode syntax in a cancellable worker. The matching deadline is REA_REGEX_MATCHING_DEADLINE_MS (a positive decimal integer of milliseconds from 1 to 2147483647, default 5000). Unset keeps the default. A deadline failure names the effective milliseconds, source (default or setting), the default, and the maximum, and leaves the API usable. The worker old-generation request is REA_REGEX_WORKER_HEAP_REQUEST_MIB (a decimal integer of mebibytes from 7 to 16384, default 128). Unset keeps the default. A positive Node --max-old-space-size, including NODE_OPTIONS, overrides that request and is not limited by the setting's floor or maximum. A heap failure names the effective request, its source (default or setting), the default, the floor, and the maximum. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: search_strings
tools.title: Search Strings
tools.description: Search every provider-reported string object or candidate using literal matching by default or regex when requested. Results are deterministic and complete over that provider inventory, not every text sequence in artifact bytes. Kuna scans mapped sequences of at least five characters, including unterminated fragments, without computing references. Ghidra may omit packed or undefined literals, including Rust strings; an empty result does not prove text is absent. If an address is known, read_bytes and xrefs inspect its bytes and references. Hopper retains typed byte decoding, native display, and explicit decoding unknowns. Adjacent long-literal fragments match independently. Hopper regex mode uses ECMAScript Unicode syntax in a cancellable worker. The matching deadline is REA_REGEX_MATCHING_DEADLINE_MS (a positive decimal integer of milliseconds from 1 to 2147483647, default 5000). Unset keeps the default. A deadline failure names the effective milliseconds, source (default or setting), the default, and the maximum, and leaves the API usable. The worker old-generation request is REA_REGEX_WORKER_HEAP_REQUEST_MIB (a decimal integer of mebibytes from 7 to 16384, default 128). Unset keeps the default. A positive Node --max-old-space-size, including NODE_OPTIONS, overrides that request and is not limited by the setting's floor or maximum. A heap failure names the effective request, its source (default or setting), the default, the floor, and the maximum. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: set_address_name
tools.title: Set Address Name
tools.description: Assign an analyst name to one mapped hexadecimal address and report whether the native edit succeeded and exact readback matched. Hopper rejects symbol names exceeding 1024 UTF-16 code units before mutation, and rejects names owned by another address; use set_addresses_names to explicitly move or swap labels among selected addresses. This mutates analysis metadata.

tools.name: set_addresses_names
tools.title: Set Addresses Names
tools.description: Assign analyst names to multiple mapped addresses in one call and return per-address edit/readback success booleans. Hopper validates mapped destinations, native string representations, its 1024 UTF-16 code-unit symbol-name limit, and unique destinations/names before applying edits. Existing labels may move or swap only among explicitly selected addresses; unselected label owners remain unchanged. This mutates analysis metadata; verify failures individually.

tools.name: set_bookmark
tools.title: Set Bookmark
tools.description: Create or update a bookmark at a mapped hexadecimal address and report readback success. Omit name to preserve an existing name or create an unnamed bookmark; an empty string clears the bookmark name. This mutates navigation metadata; bookmarks are analyst-authored navigation aids, not binary evidence.

tools.name: set_comment
tools.title: Set Comment
tools.description: Write a regular analysis comment at a hexadecimal address and return whether readback matched. An empty comment clears it. This mutates the Hopper document; use comments to record evidence IDs or reasoning.

tools.name: set_inline_comment
tools.title: Set Inline Comment
tools.description: Write an inline instruction comment at a hexadecimal address and return whether readback matched. An empty comment clears it; Hopper may flatten newlines, producing false on exact readback. This mutates analysis metadata.

tools.name: unset_bookmark
tools.title: Unset Bookmark
tools.description: Remove the bookmark at a mapped hexadecimal address and return whether it is absent. Hopper also permits removing an existing legacy bookmark outside mapped memory. This mutates navigation metadata and does not alter binary bytes.

tools.name: xrefs
tools.title: Xrefs
tools.description: Return analyzed references to a code or data address. Hopper may default to its current cursor; headless providers such as Ghidra require an explicit address. Use to connect strings, globals, selectors, and functions; bare addresses are untyped and indirect references may be incomplete. Use inspect_native_instruction at the target address for typed incoming references where supported.

tools.name: trace_native_values
tools.title: Trace Native Values
tools.description: Trace a bounded static dependency graph from one explicit native procedure. Includes high-p-code def-use, constants, operators, memory and branch operations, resolved call edges, and derived argument/parameter and return/output bindings. Missing bindings, alias semantics, persistent state and RNG roles remain unknown. Budgets bound depth, decompilations, graph size and payloads; nodes are paginated. A Ghidra per-function timeout does not bound the whole traversal; allow startup, every attempted function and other work, or reduce max_functions.

tools.name: inspect_native_dispatch_metadata
tools.title: Inspect Native Dispatch Metadata
tools.description: Inspect the bound provider's name inventory for Objective-C class/method symbols and Swift mangled symbols, returning at most max_records decoded names. Optional objc_class_import_addresses request exact pointer-slot binding facts for those addresses; they are decoded only from the selected Mach-O slice and retain partial or unsupported coverage when not established. Includes target SHA-256 when available, provider identity/version, analysis-profile digest, facet coverage, and per-record Evidence. This is static symbol and metadata evidence, not runtime metadata: ivar layouts, protocol conformances, witness/class tables, and relative pointers are explicitly marked unsupported unless a provider supplies those decoders. The provider controls how its name inventory is acquired. The Mach-O byte reader holds the whole file in memory: max_input_bytes (default 64 MiB, at most 1 GiB) bounds it, and results record input_admission.

tools.name: get_objc_classes
tools.title: Get Objc Classes
tools.description: Discover Objective-C class labels, optionally filtering by literal substring. Rows are coalesced only when exact selected-image pointer-fixup evidence proves that their own addresses bind the same imported class symbol, binding stream, raw library ordinal and resolved library, weak status, and addend. Rows without that evidence remain separate, with identity coverage reported as unknown, partial, or unsupported.

tools.name: get_objc_protocols
tools.title: Get Objc Protocols
tools.description: Discover and deduplicate Objective-C and Swift protocol labels.

tools.name: batch_decompile
tools.title: Batch Decompile
tools.description: Decompile each explicit procedure symbol or address, with one provider read active per batch. Preserves each input selector in address and reports the observed canonical entry and entry label in procedure; identity or label failures remain explicit without discarding usable pseudocode. Returns ordered per-item success or error results and aggregate counts. The complete reply retains every pseudocode body; use selected small batches to bound retained output. A per-function limit is not a batch deadline; allow for every item or split calls.

tools.name: decompile_all
tools.title: Decompile All
tools.description: Write provider pseudocode for every analyzed function, or a filtered subset, into a caller-selected directory and return only a manifest. Each file records the provider function name, canonical address, inclusive body ranges when procedure_info supplies them, and that function's procedure_info and pseudocode limitations. Each function's index record keeps its complete limitations. Evidence keeps at most eight first-observed distinct per-function limitations within an encoded-text budget; the omitted count measures observations, not distinct warnings. The manifest reports counts, the output directory, the index path, at most 32 failure details within 2,048 JSON-encoded UTF-8 bytes (names can be omitted; full names remain in the index), provider identity, and the analysis-profile digest. Pseudocode stays in the files. An existing directory is refused unless resume is set and the journal matches the target SHA-256, provider, and analysis profile; verified files are skipped and conflicting files are left unchanged. layout dwarf reports that compilation-unit paths are unavailable and names files by address. A failure of one function does not stop the others. Functions procedure_info classifies as external are counted as external, get no file, and are not decompiled; a resume skips them. Cancellation leaves files already written. Per-function limits do not bound the whole call; use limit and resume to select work that fits the client deadline, including import, listing and file work.

output_directory.description: Absolute output directory. The parent must exist. The directory itself must be absent unless resume is true. One run at a time may use a directory; a second run is refused while the first holds it.

layout.description: address names files by canonical address. dwarf asks for compilation-unit paths and is reported unavailable when the provider has no such fact.

resume.description: Continue a journal for the same target SHA-256, provider, analysis profile, and layout. Both digests must be known. Verified files and functions recorded as external are skipped, conflicting files are left unchanged, and functions not yet tried run before retries of recorded failures.

name.description: Case-sensitive literal substring of the provider function name.

namespace.description: Case-sensitive prefix of the provider function name, including any separator such as Foo:: or Class.

address_start.description: Inclusive lower bound as 0xoffset or space:0xoffset. Must use the same address space as address_end.

address_end.description: Inclusive upper bound as 0xoffset or space:0xoffset. Must use the same address space as address_start.

limit.description: Maximum functions to attempt on this call after skipping verified files and functions recorded as external. Further matches remain for a later resume.

inputSchema.description: Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

tools.name: get_call_graph
tools.title: Get Call Graph
tools.description: Resolve one symbol or address to its canonical procedure entry, then traverse the bound provider's caller or callee relationships until the reachable graph is exhausted. Every node uses a canonical address and has an ok/error status; failures use safe typed projections. Unresolved indirect calls may be missing and results are not a whole-program CFG.

tools.name: analyze_swift_types
tools.title: Analyze Swift Types
tools.description: Categorize analyzed Swift procedure names using their manglings or same-address Swift symbol aliases. Decodes legacy and literal modern nominal contexts into classes, structs, enums, protocols, and extensions. Preserves provider names and supporting mangled_names; unresolved categories appear in other and in unclassified, which remains inline even under category filters. Returns deduplicated procedure-name counts, not unique source types, plus identification limitations. Optionally select one category and/or apply a case-sensitive literal filter to provider names or supporting manglings; for example, use {category: "structs", pattern: "Pair"}.

tools.name: find_xrefs_to_name
tools.title: Find Xrefs To Name
tools.description: Resolve an exact name against the bound provider's name inventory and return a resolved or unresolved result. Unresolved names use the stable name_not_found reason; this xref workflow returns address-only projections.

tools.name: binary_overview
tools.title: Binary Overview
tools.description: Return the bound document and exhaustive procedure/string counts, plus every segment and segment_count when the provider supports segment enumeration. If segment fields are omitted, segment coverage is unavailable rather than empty. When every observed segment agrees on an analysis image base, return it as image_base so callers can relate provider addresses to their loader coordinates. Use search_procedures, list_procedures, or analyze_function directly when you already know which procedure to inspect.

tools.name: analyze_function
tools.title: Analyze Function
tools.description: Build a dossier for one native function identified by symbol or provider-returned address. Returns identity with complete inclusive analyzed body ranges or explicit unknown, provider-specific pseudocode and assembly, comments, calls, references, referenced strings/names, local CFG blocks, and available native API boundary observations. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in limitations with available callee identities. Default detail summary returns a compact dossier (identity, pseudocode size, facet counts, value-flow availability) and retains the complete dossier Evidence in this session; page pseudocode, references, assembly and value-flow through normalized_result.parent_evidence_id with inspect_analysis_view. detail complete returns the full dossier inline.

tools.name: inspect_native_api
tools.title: Inspect Native Api
tools.description: Analyze a native API boundary in one function identified by symbol or provider-returned address. Returns confidence, evidence, jump-table dispatch/data/case mappings, separately evidenced default targets, unsupported branches, and residual unknowns. Null case values mean unresolved cases, never a known default.

tools.name: trace_feature
tools.title: Trace Feature
tools.description: Trace the complete literal query, preserving spaces, through every matching string and procedure, their xrefs, and truthful containing-procedure resolution. Returns observations and residual unknowns without inferring reference kinds.

tools.name: trace_call_path
tools.title: Trace Call Path
tools.description: Resolve start and optional goal symbols or addresses to canonical procedure entries, then trace direct callers or callees until the graph is exhausted or the goal is reached. Results use canonical addresses; Evidence preserves supplied selectors. Returns visited nodes, direct-call edges, a shortest traversal path, provider failures, and residual unknowns. A requested goal is unknown when unresolved expansions prevent proving it absent; unresolved indirect calls remain unknown.

tools.name: trace_native_ui_action
tools.title: Trace Native Ui Action
tools.description: Trace one unique compiled UI action, object ID, native symbol or exact function address through authored connections, encoded or symbolized Objective-C handlers, and bounded static call references. Typed direct and resolved indirect calls, ambiguous candidates, inferred untyped provider callees, and targetless sites remain distinct. Runtime reachability is unknown; use trace_native_values for recovered value dependencies.

tools.name: observe_native_ui
tools.title: Observe Native Ui
tools.description: Observe an already-running native app by PID and window ID, bound to the active Mach-O target. Captures a bounded accessibility tree and selected-window screenshot; OS permission denial fails without broad capture or target launch. native_ui_deadline_ms is the observation deadline (omitted means 180000 ms, range 1..2147483647, next call). It does not raise the fixed 67108864-byte output allowance or the 180000 ms wait-step cap.

tools.name: capture_native_ui_scenario
tools.title: Capture Native Ui Scenario
tools.description: Run selected-element press, increment/decrement scroll, AXValue text entry and bounded wait steps in one exact native app window. Returns ordered before/after captures and action/capture failures. Actions can change app data, network activity and persistent state; application state is left as-is and restoration is not attempted. native_ui_deadline_ms is the scenario deadline (omitted means 180000 ms, range 1..2147483647, next call). It does not raise the fixed 67108864-byte output allowance or the 180000 ms wait-step cap.

max_nodes.description: Maximum accessibility nodes per capture; increase for large windows.

native_ui_deadline_ms.description: Deadline in milliseconds for this UI observation or scenario, including helper preparation and captures. Omitted means 180000. Integer from 1 to 2147483647. Applies on the next call. Does not raise the fixed 67108864-byte scenario output allowance or the 180000 ms cap on one wait step. A partial observation may already be retained when this deadline expires.

inputSchema.description: Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

tools.name: observe_native_calls
tools.title: Observe Native Calls
tools.description: Launch the active Mach-O as an owned process under LLDB and record each entry into caller-selected functions or Objective-C methods: thread, module, symbol, load and file address, raw argument registers, selector, receiver class and optional caller frames. Every hit auto-continues. No expression is evaluated and no other process is attached. The process is killed when max_events or duration_ms is reached; exit status, captured stdout/stderr, unresolved breakpoints and limitations are returned inline. The process runs with the current user's permissions and may change files, show UI or use the network. A hardened-runtime target needs the get-task-allow entitlement.

environment.description: Overrides on top of the environment REA runs with.

tools.name: inspect_plist
tools.title: Inspect Plist
tools.description: Requires an open binary or bundle-resource session; use open_binary or open_bundle_resources first. The 4096-byte markup probe is a probe window, not a document cap, and has no runtime override.

Omitted means 60000. Integer from 1 to 2147483647. Applies on the next call. Does not raise the fixed 67108864-byte output allowance or the 65536-byte failure-diagnostic excerpt. tools.name: inspect_artifact
tools.title: Inspect Artifact
tools.description: Inspect an active archive or application package, including Node.js SEA carriers, in one call. By default returns the complete content-addressed artifact graph once, as the typed nested inventory Evidence, with root and integrity observations, integrity contradictions, hypotheses, unexplored branches, limitations, and next probes inline. For PCK and large containers prefer detail summary: it retains the complete inspection and returns its derived summary view; read exact paths, batch occurrence/content IDs and selected fields with inspect_analysis_view using parent_evidence_id. This changes delivery, not inventory coverage. Read-only DMG mounting is used automatically on supported macOS hosts. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue keeps mismatches explicitly untrusted. It does not extract files; use extract_artifact to materialize regular contents of supported formats. DMG extraction is unavailable; use a caller-managed read-only mount on macOS to access its files.

tools.name: extract_artifact
tools.title: Extract Artifact
tools.description: Extract regular files (including Node.js SEA scripts and assets) exposed by a supported active archive reader into a fresh temporary directory chosen by REA. A nested archive exposed as a file is copied as a file; inspect and extract it separately to unpack its contents. The result includes its location. DMG extraction is unavailable; use a caller-managed read-only mount on macOS to access its files. Rejects traversal and symlink escapes, never overwrites, and verifies cleanup. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue extracts the observed bytes and returns each mismatch as an explicitly untrusted integrity contradiction.

tools.name: decode_interface_builder
tools.title: Decode Interface Builder
tools.description: Decode compiled storyboard and nib archives inside the active Apple app bundle, including keyed property lists and NIBArchive object tables, into a bounded object, hierarchy, and connection graph. This is static archive parsing; unrecognized archive classes and unresolved code handlers remain explicit unknowns. A full app graph is often several megabytes; detail summary retains it and returns documents with node, edge and coverage counts, then page rows, optionally one document's, with inspect_analysis_view kind interface-builder.

tools.name: inspect_keyed_archive
tools.title: Inspect Keyed Archive
tools.description: Inspect one Foundation NSKeyedArchiver plist in the active app bundle as original object-table nodes, class descriptors, named roots, and UID edges. Preserves shared and cyclic references without instantiating classes. The path is relative to the bundle; root selection and object pagination preserve original identities.

tools.name: inspect_asset_catalog
tools.title: Inspect Asset Catalog
tools.description: Inspect compiled Assets.car metadata in an active Apple app bundle. Returns stable paginated catalog and rendition records with raw assetutil metadata and catalog digests; rendition bytes are not extracted.

tools.name: trace_dylib_resolution
tools.title: Trace Dylib Resolution
tools.description: Trace how dyld would resolve each Mach-O dylib load for the active Mach-O, or for every executable in the active .app bundle (the main app, XPC services, extensions, login items, helpers). Expands @executable_path, @loader_path, and @rpath through each process's LC_RPATH stack in dependents-first load order, and reports every candidate path with its outcome, the resolved image and digest, weak, re-export, upward, and lazy-load flags, including LC_LAZY_LOAD_DYLIB_INFO linkedit payloads, and derived findings such as unresolved required loads or absent earlier @rpath candidates. Pure header parsing: nothing is executed, and absolute or system paths outside the analyzed root stay undetermined. Select roots or one architecture to narrow large bundles.

tools.name: inspect_managed_artifact
tools.title: Inspect Managed Artifact
tools.description: Inspect an explicit PE/CLI path, or the selected managed target, without loading or executing target code. Omitted or complete detail returns complete metadata inventories with original coverage. Select detail: "summary" on the first call for complete identity, PE/CLI, classification with its evidence, module/MVID, assembly, frameworks, returned-collection counts, coverage/issues and limitations. It retains complete Evidence and returns a distinct linked inspect_analysis_view summary. Page original references/resources/attributes with view kind managed and normalized_result.parent_evidence_id. Counts cover producer-returned rows; partial, unavailable or malformed metadata remains explicit and tokens remain build-local.

tools.name: inspect_managed_members
tools.title: Inspect Managed Members
tools.description: Inspect PE/CLI metadata members, signatures, raw CIL hashes, decoded-instruction-tuple hashes, separately reported exception regions, call edges, field-access anchors, and the #US string literals that ldstr loads, without loading or executing target code. Select type_names to decode only the members of those exact declaring types and the literals their bodies load, which keeps large assemblies such as a base class library within the representation budget. Metadata tokens are reported as build-local coordinates bound to the artifact SHA-256 and MVID; the tuple hash does not resolve them or fully commit control flow. Omitted or complete detail returns every collection, including the assembly-wide member_refs and exported_types, which type_names does not narrow. Select detail: "summary" for identity, metadata status, selection with unmatched names, coverage/issues, limitations and per-collection counts; it retains complete Evidence and returns a linked inspect_analysis_view summary. Page original rows with view kind managed-members, normalized_result.parent_evidence_id and collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings.

tools.name: inspect_managed_native_boundaries
tools.title: Inspect Managed Native Boundaries
tools.description: Inspect PE/CLI ModuleRef, ImplMap/PInvoke declarations, CLI native-header indicators, and non-IL method implementation flags without loading or executing target code. Results are managed declarations and degraded native-boundary observations, not verified native exports or addresses.

tools.name: compare_managed_members
tools.title: Compare Managed Members
tools.description: Compare two authenticated inspect_managed_members Evidence records using unique-only tiers: exact declared type, name, and CIL/signature; exact declared type, name, and signature (decoded or not); exact declared type, name, and decoded structural method shape; then exact CIL/signature or decoded structural method shape alone, which never takes a member whose own declared type and name remain unpaired on the other side or whose declaring type is unresolved. Signatures compare type operands by name, not by build-local metadata row. Names alone are never a matching basis; a member whose signature was not decoded, or whose same-named counterpart's was not, stays unknown rather than added or removed. Matched methods also compare aligned call-site shapes and observed target declaring-type/method names; missing or unaligned call edges and target names remain unknown. These static names do not prove overload identity or runtime dispatch. Metadata tokens remain build-local coordinates bound to each artifact SHA-256 and MVID, and the tuple digest does not itself remap them.

tools.name: inspect_with_objdump
tools.title: Inspect With Objdump
tools.description: Run caller-selected GNU objdump inspection against a local artifact, or request operation=architectures without a path to list BFD targets advertised by the installed binary. For operation=disassemble, optional symbol selects native symbol-scoped disassembly before output collection; omission preserves all code sections. Matching and symbol boundaries follow GNU objdump. Preserves decoded stdout and stderr inline with SHA-256 Evidence for artifact inspections, up to a shared 16 MiB combined limit; invalid UTF-8 bytes are represented by replacement characters and flagged in Evidence limitations. output_truncated reports output beyond that limit and completion_status is unknown if buffer enforcement terminated the process. The raw output is authoritative and REA does not claim a stable normalized format. DWARF does not follow local debug links by default. Set follow_debug_links to true to follow them; identities of external debug files are not bound to Evidence. REA clears DEBUGINFOD_URLS for objdump so DWARF processing does not make debuginfod network requests. Default detail complete returns original Evidence. Explicit detail summary retains the complete parent and returns its command observation once, without the raw mirror; parent_evidence_id supports later inspect_analysis_view summary queries and complete Evidence export. Architecture output is subjectless and does not establish support for any artifact. Optional command_timeout_ms is the per-phase wall clock in milliseconds (default 120000, range 1..2147483647); omitted means 120000 and the value applies on the next call. It does not raise the 16 MiB output cap.

tools.name: execute_rizin_command
tools.title: Execute Rizin Command
tools.description: Execute one caller-selected Rizin command against a local artifact using the Rizin CLI profile that suppresses user settings and scripts while retaining plugins. Preserves decoded stdout and stderr inline with SHA-256 Evidence, up to a shared 16 MiB combined limit; invalid UTF-8 bytes are represented by replacement characters and flagged in Evidence limitations. output_truncated reports output beyond that limit and completion_status is unknown if buffer enforcement terminated the process. Rizin commands and retained plugins can execute foreign code, mutate files, access the network, and read files outside the selected artifact; identities and contents of those external inputs are not bound to Evidence. Command effects depend on the Rizin command and loaded plugins; JSON is command-specific and raw output remains authoritative. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first. Optional command_timeout_ms is the per-phase wall clock in milliseconds (default 120000, range 1..2147483647); omitted means 120000 and the value applies on the next call. It does not raise the 16 MiB output cap or a Rizin debugger session deadline.

tools.name: start_frida_session
tools.title: Start Frida Session

tools.name: load_frida_script
tools.title: Load Frida Script

tools.name: resume_frida_session

tools.name: unload_frida_script

tools.name: frida_session_status
tools.title: Frida Session Status

Default detail=complete returns queued script messages and capture truncation. detail=summary retains the complete observation in this session and returns identity, state, scripts, retained message count and truncation without payloads. Export the complete parent with export_evidence_bundle; retained summaries are historical and never refresh live state.

tools.name: close_frida_session
tools.title: Close Frida Session
tools.description: Unload session scripts and attempt to detach REA's Frida session. Then resume a still-paused spawned process if script cleanup or session detach confirms instrumentation was released. Cleanup failures are reported. REA never kills the target; its final state is reported as unknown.

tools.name: instrument_with_frida
tools.title: Instrument With Frida
tools.description: Run one caller-authored Frida script against an explicitly selected process and detach when the observation window ends. The CLI and MCP share this ephemeral workflow; use MCP session operations for persistent sessions. Remote authentication is used only for this call and excluded from Evidence.

tools.name: list_cutter_sessions
tools.title: List Cutter Sessions
tools.description: List live REA bridge sessions hosted by upstream Cutter instances, including observed document identity and bridge-directory security status. Discovery admits at most 256 descriptor candidates (16 MiB at the descriptor byte limit). That candidate budget is separate from REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES and has no runtime override. Discovery reads and probes at most eight concurrently, and reports bridge_directory_capacity_exceeded rather than claiming no sessions when that budget is exceeded.

tools.name: cutter_command
tools.title: Cutter Command
tools.description: Run one arbitrary Rizin command in a selected live Cutter session. Commands may edit and persist analysis state or execute plugin-provided effects; completion uncertainty is returned as Evidence and must not be retried automatically. The authenticated request and response frame is bounded by REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (default 16777216 bytes, floor 7464, maximum 536870887). The payload budget excludes the terminating LF. An out-of-band Cutter process without the setting uses 16777216 bytes; a mismatch is refused before the command is sent. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: start_gdb_session
tools.title: Start Gdb Session
tools.description: Start a BYO GDB process in MI3 mode when available, suppress startup files, and disable auto-loading. Persistent GDB sessions are available only on Linux, where REA can verify live inferior output descriptors through /proc before detaching; macOS descriptor verification is not implemented, and Windows Job Object cleanup can terminate debugger inferiors. Optionally set inferior_tty to a caller-selected terminal for future inferior runs; REA verifies the setting through GDB/MI before the session becomes ready. The selected terminal must remain available after GDB exits. A live inferior can be detached during close only while this durable output sink remains verified. The session persists in this REA MCP server process and receives an explicit session ID.

tools.name: gdb_console
tools.title: Gdb Console
tools.description: Run one unrestricted GDB CLI command through MI interpreter-exec console and return raw MI, console, target, and log records inline with Evidence. Default detail complete preserves the original Evidence. Explicit detail summary retains that complete parent and returns every ordered MI record once, omitting duplicate stream groupings and raw mirrors; parent_evidence_id supports later inspect_analysis_view summary queries and complete Evidence export. A command timeout preserves collected records with completion_status unknown and stops the owned debugger session. Commands can execute shell, alter target state, access files, and use network. Closing the debugger never implies target termination. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: gdb_session_status
tools.title: Gdb Session Status
tools.description: Return the observed lifecycle state and bounded recent MI records and process diagnostics for one persistent REA GDB session; truncation and invalid-UTF-8 fields report discarded or lossy data.

tools.name: close_gdb_session
tools.title: Close Gdb Session
tools.description: Close the owned GDB process after verifying the inferior state. When one live thread group has a verified durable output TTY, REA automatically detaches it, which may resume target execution; otherwise close reports that a disposition is required. REA never kills attached or remote targets as part of debugger cleanup. In a shared MCP server, this admitted close retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: start_rizin_debug_session
tools.title: Start Rizin Debug Session
tools.description: Start a persistent Rizin debugger session using `-N` to suppress user settings and scripts while retaining plugins, `-0` for NUL framing, and `-d` with an optional caller-selected IO debugger backend. Requires a caller-selected Linux TTY for inferior stdout and stderr; the target may write directly to that terminal while running and after detach. REA verifies both destinations and `dbg.exitkills=false` before detaching. Backend and target capabilities depend on the installed build. The session lives in this REA MCP process. Persistent sessions require Linux `/proc` descriptor readback. In a shared MCP server, starting this session retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: rizin_debug_command
tools.title: Rizin Debug Command
tools.description: Execute one unrestricted command in a persistent Rizin debugger session. Returns raw output inline with Evidence, including backend output interleaved before the completion marker. If the command exceeds the output-byte, frame-byte, or frame-count limit, `output_truncated` is true and `completion_status` is `unknown`; retained partial output is returned and the owned debugger session is stopped. Evidence names the cap that stopped capture. Unsolicited frames already queued before the command make the session unavailable because correlation is ambiguous. Commands can access local files, shell, network, plugins, and target state; effects depend on the active backend and target. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

tools.name: rizin_debug_session_status
tools.title: Rizin Debug Session Status
tools.description: Return observed lifecycle state and bounded recent NUL-framed output and process diagnostics for one Rizin debugger session; truncation fields report discarded data, and output_invalid_utf8 reports whether invalid UTF-8 has been observed in session frame bytes; recent output may contain replacement characters.

tools.name: close_rizin_debug_session
tools.title: Close Rizin Debug Session
tools.description: Close the REA-owned Rizin debugger only after verifying no inferior remains or detaching one with a verified caller-selected TTY output sink. A detached target may continue running and write to that TTY; target state is otherwise reported as unknown. REA never signals an inferior based on PID or path. In a shared MCP server, this admitted close retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

Optional packet_limit counts input packets before filtering; output paging does not shorten dissection or two-pass reassembly. Requires Linux, util-linux prlimit, and TShark 4.x on PATH or through absolute REA_TSHARK_COMMAND. File-only analysis; no live capture or device communication. Missing fields or no matches do not establish absence of device traffic.

tools.name: inspect_jeb_client
tools.title: Inspect Jeb Client
tools.description: Inspect the running JEB client serving MCP: engine version, GUI or headless mode, and startup time. Does not open a target. Requires a caller-started JEB client reachable at REA_JEB_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8425/mcp); REA never installs or launches JEB.

tools.name: open_jeb_project
tools.title: Open Jeb Project
tools.description: Open or create a JEB project from an artifact file or existing .jdb2 database on the engine host. Returns the project's input-file digests and top-level units. The engine analyzes the target itself; REA does not read the file or execute it. Fails when a project is already open.

tools.name: list_jeb_units
tools.title: List Jeb Units
tools.description: List project units by stable unit path and type, with optional wildcard filter, parent restriction, and pagination. The engine caps pages at 100 units; a full page reports partial coverage because more units may exist. Read-only.

tools.name: decompile_jeb_item
tools.title: Decompile Jeb Item
tools.description: Decompile one type or method to engine pseudo-code using its decompiler (Dalvik, Java, or native). item_address comes from the engine's code item listing; unit_path defaults to the engine's first code unit and stays unknown when omitted. Read-only with respect to the target file.

tools.name: inspect_byte_entropy
tools.title: Inspect Byte Entropy
tools.description: Inspect Shannon byte entropy for one explicit local file offline, without execution, extraction or external tools. Returns file-wide SHA-256 and entropy, fixed-block entropy for an optional offset/length window, and adjacent high (>=7.2) and low (<=1.0) runs with exact file offsets. Block size is a power of two from 256 to 65536 (default 4096). Complete output can become very large because it includes one row per selected block, and summary detail still retains that full list. Use a shorter length or a larger block_size; the selected window is limited to 32,768 output blocks. Entropy cannot distinguish compression from encryption. Summary detail returns file entropy plus the ten longest runs; retrieve parent Evidence for the full series. The entire file is read even for a window.

tools.name: inspect_binary_layout
tools.title: Inspect Binary Layout
tools.description: Inspect an explicit local binary without launching it as a host process. Returns file-backed section/segment ranges, linked addresses, original symbol/REL/RELA table identities, complete encoded RELR tables and upstream-derived offsets with unknown per-word locations/addends, raw name bytes, dependency/interpreter names and static mitigation inferences inline with artifact SHA-256 Evidence. Profile: EXEC/DYN/REL ELF64 x86-64, ELF32 i386, ELF32 little-endian ARM and ELF32 little- or big-endian MIPS on Linux x64 via caller-supplied Python with unchanged pwntools 4.15.0, pyelftools 0.33 and Unicorn 2.1.2. Runtime addresses/library paths, overall relocation inventory completeness and complete derived GOT/PLT coverage remain unknown. Zero executable entry values mean absence; relocatable entries are not applicable. Upstream can emulate PLT instructions with Unicorn for derived static maps. Uses bounded complete output and owned temporary files/processes; malformed, unsupported or oversized objects return no partial success. Select detail summary to retain the complete layout Evidence in this session and receive only its summary view, then inspect sections, symbols, mitigations or linkage with inspect_analysis_view. pwntools_timeout_ms is each owned pwntools command's deadline (omitted means 30000 ms, range 1..2147483647, next call). cpuSeconds 30 and the output, diagnostic, and address-space byte allowances have no runtime override.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path to the selected binary

pwntools_timeout_ms.description: Deadline in milliseconds for each owned pwntools command in this call. Omitted means 30000. Integer from 1 to 2147483647. Applies on the next call. Does not raise cpuSeconds 30 or the output (67108864 bytes), diagnostic (1048576 bytes), or address-space (3221225472 bytes) allowances. Artifact admission stays REA_PWNTOOLS_MAX_INPUT_BYTES (default 33554432 bytes).

detail.description: complete returns the complete analysis Evidence inline. summary retains that complete Evidence in this session and returns its inspect_analysis_view summary; inspect pages, items or facets through normalized_result.parent_evidence_id.

tools.name: inspect_analysis_view
tools.title: Inspect Analysis View
tools.description: Use javascript-routes collections to query route patterns, source-linked occurrences, source status, unknowns or summary counts from retained JavaScript application or web-bundle Evidence. Inspect selected views of supported completed Evidence without repeating analysis. Choose a view compatible with the parent operation described below. Command summary views preserve ordered GDB records or opaque objdump stdout/stderr once, source parameters, completion facts and parent identity. They do not establish current target state. Historical capture summaries return identity and counts without bodies or archive inventories. Capture views page retained records: view {kind: "capture", detail: "preview" | "complete", offset: 0, limit: 20}; preview selects recorded headline fields and binary descriptors, complete returns exact records with all sidecars. Offsets follow the selected parent record order, preserving original producer ordinals. Paging never reopens the source or reruns the decoder. Native export tables use kind native-exports, collection exports/issues, exact names or original indices, selected fields and matching-row pagination; parent Evidence plus source_index identifies each row. Source coverage stays separate from page coverage. BEAM views use kind beam, collections atoms/exports/imports/lambdas/chunks, exact names/indices/fields and matching-row pages; import modules intersects function names. source_index identifies original parent-and-collection rows, preserving every arity and raw atom index. beam.counts preserves null missing tables versus decoded empty tables; runtime absence remains unknown. PYC views use kind python-pyc, collection code_objects, names/indices/fields and paging; source_index scopes every same-name alternative to the parent, nested_code keeps code-constant references, and pyc.coverage preserves source coverage. Go metadata uses kind go, collection dependencies/settings, exact paths/keys or indices, fields and pagination. Row index refers to the original collection; empty selections return no rows, and dependency coverage remains unknown. Rust metadata uses kind rust, collection packages/edges, exact names/versions or original indices, selected fields, edge from_indices/to_indices and matching-row pagination. Embedded-record coverage is separate from unknown runtime dependencies. For inspect_pcap_capture parents, kind pcap pages endpoints, dns-queries, tls-sni, protocols, http-uris or unattributed-addresses. Select an exact query for dns-addresses, or a tshark/capinfos stream for UTF-16 diagnostics text. Page totals count retained facts; source coverage remains explicit. Qlog summaries keep profile/scope and counts; kind qlog pages traces, streams, loss-declarations, incomplete-records, contributions, ranges or final-sizes. Except traces, select trace_index; stream-specific facets also require exact stream_id and direction. Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope, and interval overlap or endpoint loss declarations do not prove retransmission or network loss. The api-surface view groups retained HAR requests by method, origin and format-rule path template; templated segments are inferences. It reads no headers or bodies and reports no query values. The environment-manifest view projects the same HAR requests on the primary origin (most JSON-like records) into a replayable tool surface: view {kind: "environment-manifest", template_rules: ["after-uid-literal", "opaque-token", "sibling-variance"], include_query_parameter_names: true}. Each tool has a deterministic name, a path template and parameters from the four format rules plus the selected opt-in rules, observed query parameter names, a value-free body shape for POST/PUT/PATCH, status and content-type sets and record ordinals; records are pointers into the parent, excluded groups carry a reason and three fixed unknowns are always stated. Templates, parameters and names are inferences; the view copies no header, cookie or body values and refuses parents inspected with sensitive values. A capture_browser_scenario parent that selected response bodies or header values projects the same way, one record per network transaction in request order; it relies on capture-time redaction of declared secrets instead of that refusal, and a transaction whose URL was redacted is left unrepresented. The environment-state view extracts, from the same parents, the initial state the recorded reads observed: view {kind: "environment-state", template_rules: [...]} with the rules of the manifest it accompanies. It reads response bodies recorded before the first related write and reports entity types with an identity field (proved by a path parameter or inferred from a field name), entities in collection order with per-view values where views differ, documents for non-parameterized reads that are not entities and have one initial request line (item-shaped paths stay recorded), and a render plan per read tool: item and list views reproduce their latest recordings from the state (a list also learns the filters, search, sort and paging its recordings verify, and answers new values of them from the state), and every other read tool is a recorded view with a reason. It also reports a write plan per state-changing tool (create, update, delete or document, built from its first successful call) and write_clock; a plan is served only when replaying the capture shows a later read confirming its effect and none contradicting it. Types and identity are inferences; values are recorded data, so it refuses parents inspected with sensitive values, and a scenario parent must have selected response bodies; its values keep the capture redaction markers, and a write whose URL it redacted ends the state of every type. The environment-coverage view, view {kind: "environment-coverage", template_rules: [...]}, summarizes that state without its entities: reads.state and reads.recorded count read tools answered from the state and replayed (recorded_reasons per view reason), writes.served lists the served write tools, and writes.withheld lists each other write tool with its reason, plan record, contradicting read and a hint about what to record next; it refuses what the environment-state view refuses. For a retained record use source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary receipt. Source kind is required. Portable source uses {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>}. A completed Evidence JSON file on this host uses {kind: "evidence-file", path: "<absolute path>"}: REA reads and authenticates it, then projects it like retained Evidence, so a large capture is bounded by the file reader rather than by inline-input accounting. The file may also be an Evidence bundle written by CLI --evidence_output or export_evidence_bundle; select evidence_id when it contains more than one record. For layout, JavaScript, inventory, WASM, Mach-O, Interface Builder, EVM, managed artifact, Android package and Dart AOT sources, request a summary with view: {kind: "summary"}; summary is a view kind and has no facet. The WASM summary gives validation, counts, WAT digest/length, tool profile and execution/network states without reading WAT text. Select a layout mitigations/linkage facet, one section/symbol/module, or a stable page. Module pages include assets, bundled and source modules; use node_id for ambiguous or unavailable paths. Typed module references use view {kind: "javascript", collection: "modules", projection: "references", where: {path: "main.js", kind: "javascript-module"}, offset: 0, limit: 64}; where matches exact retained strings (null selects unavailable paths). Rows include canonical identity, retained source-range count and observation support states. Source coverage and selection remain explicit; exhausting matching rows does not prove runtime loading or complete analysis. For exact file/native facts and processing gaps, use view {kind: "javascript-facts", where: {paths: ["package.json"]}, property_keys: ["name", "operation", "analysis_status"]}. Rows page original observations with canonical identities and Evidence; missing properties remain omitted. Paths match recorded artifact-path/source-range locations; optional kinds filter nodes. To discover field names without values, opt into include_available_property_keys: true with property_keys: []. Canonical identity and Evidence are separate from properties; keep each node_id/observation_id pair together when composing results. Inventory uses view: {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json"], offset: 0, limit: 64}. Inventory views page nodes, occurrences, edges or integrity contradictions. Occurrences accept exact logical_paths and occurrence_ids; nodes accept artifact_ids. Batch filters intersect (omitted means all available, [] means none); fields selects columns while retaining identity links. source_complete describes retained graph membership; source_coverage describes producer coverage, including unknown encrypted PCK directories. Page exhaustion does not prove absence in a partial source. WASM views use kind wasm and facet sections/imports/exports/candidates/glue/wat/headers/details/tool_profile; text facets use UTF-16 code units and source forms remain exact. Mach-O views use kind macho and facet entrypoints/architectures/build_metadata/load_commands/dependencies/imports/exports/segments/provenance; source_exhaustive false means unreturned rows may exist. Interface Builder views use kind interface-builder and collection documents/nodes/edges/coverage; nodes and edges accept an exact document relative_path. EVM summary returns all inferred interface candidates, carrier/decoded identities and explicit unknowns without hex or duplicate stdout. EVM views use kind evm and facet functions/bytecode_hex/stdout/stderr; function pages preserve the original candidate rows, and text offsets/limits count UTF-16 code units (hex has two characters per decoded byte). Exhausting candidate pages does not establish global interface completeness. Managed artifact summaries preserve complete identity/classification, metadata status, module/MVID, frameworks, coverage and limitations without unrelated inventories. Managed pages use kind managed and collection references/resources/attributes, retaining source coverage and build-local token scope; page exhaustion does not establish complete metadata. Managed member summaries keep identity, selection with unmatched names, coverage and per-collection counts; managed-members pages use collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings and carry the source selection and coverage. Android package summaries retain all declarations, engine identity and counts without decoded manifest text. Android manifest pages use kind android, facet manifest, offset and limit in UTF-16 code units; source_status preserves partial decoded coverage even when the retained text page is exhausted. Dart AOT summary preserves target/ABI/library identity, snapshot headers and pool lower bounds. String pages use kind dart-aot, collection package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens; source coverage remains partial when the producer says partial. Protobuf views use kind protobuf, collection bodies/frames/fields, with record_ordinals, body_pointers and fields; field pages also select frame_indices, field_ids, field_numbers or schema_names. Byte identity, offset basis and body status remain present. Text and schema_value are opt-in page columns. APK signing views use kind apk-signature and collection signers/digests/lineage, with ids, signer_ids, schemes, fields and paging. Identity links remain when fields is empty. Declared identities and digest matches do not establish signature verification or authenticity. Model views use kind model-artifact and collection metadata (keys), tensors (names/types) or types (derived totals), with indices, fields and paging. Header SHA-256 scopes declarations; full-file identity remains unknown unless full hashing was selected. Arrays retain typed eight-element previews with explicit omissions. IL2CPP metadata views use kind il2cpp-metadata and collection sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/string_literals/code_gen_modules/method_addresses/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances/generic_method_issues. Select indices, fields and pages; sections/images/types/methods/fields/properties/events/parameters/return_types/field_types/parameter_types/generic_method_instances accept exact names (native type names match retained rendered values, preserving same-name rows; null names never match), types also accept image_indices/namespaces/declaring_types, and methods/members accept declaring_types. Parameters and parameter_types accept method_indices; code_gen_modules accept image_indices; method_addresses and generic_method_instances accept addresses/states (generic_method_instances also method_indices), preserving every folded alternative; generic_method_issues accept rows. Row index is scoped to the metadata digest; native pages add binary_source. Uncollected native tables have null counts and remain unavailable. Desktop directory views use kind desktop-application and collection files/omissions/candidates/components/next_probes, with fields and pagination; files and omissions accept exact paths or their stable IDs, and candidates accept families. Source coverage and stable row IDs remain available. Native inventory Evidence from list_names, list/search_procedures or list/search_strings uses view: {kind: "native-inventory", offset: 0, limit: 64, fields: ["value"]}. Rows keep source_index and address even with selected fields. Summary counts describe retained rows; provider discovery coverage remains unknown. Native function Evidence accepts kind summary for identity, availability and facet counts, or kind native for selected facts: view: {kind: "native", facet: "procedure"}. Facets select procedure, pseudocode, assembly, basic blocks, comments, callers/callees, references, unresolved calls, referenced strings/names, native API and high-pcode. Use nonnegative offset and a positive caller-selected limit (defaults 0 and 64); pseudocode uses UTF-16 code units, other native pages use rows. Returns artifact identity, parent Evidence ID, a distinct view digest, coverage, limitations and unknowns. Actual serialized size determines MCP transport admission; choose a smaller page or export the complete retained Evidence if needed.

tools.title: Inspect Devicetree
tools.description: Inspect an explicit local flattened devicetree blob (FDT v16/v17) without execution or external tools. Returns validated header, memory reservations, full node/property tree with bounded raw hex, derived standard strings, cells and parent-sized reg tuples, aliases and selected single-cell phandle references with unresolved targets. Binding-specific arrays, overlays and runtime hardware remain unknown. Malformed structure or exhausted named budgets fails without partial success. tools.name: inspect_elf_notes
tools.title: Inspect Elf Notes
tools.description: Inspect one explicit local ELF32/ELF64 image's PT_NOTE program headers and SHT_NOTE sections without executing it or opening a disassembler. Returns note-table file ranges, owners, types, descriptor SHA-256 and hex previews, plus GNU build-id, ABI-tag and gold-version fields when those descriptors match. A missing table is observed absence of those declarations, not proof the image never carried notes in another container. Reads a stable regular file; malformed ELF headers, truncated notes and exhausted budgets return no partial success. Portable on supported Node hosts; no debug package or catalog is required.

tools.name: inspect_apple_ips
tools.title: Inspect Apple Ips
tools.description: Inspect one explicit local Apple .ips crash report without executing a target, launching atos, or opening a disassembler. Parses the first-line metadata object and, when bug_type is the string 309, the crash body: process identity, exception and termination facts, threads, usedImages, lossless integer registers, and deterministic classification from documented SIGKILL, EXC_GUARD, pointer-authentication and dyld strings. Other bug_type values, including 288 stackshots, return no crash result. A missing or truncated body fails without partial success. Opened Mach-O and dSYM UUID joins remain unobserved. Portable on supported Node hosts; no Xcode or pwntools required.

tools.name: inspect_kernel_module
tools.title: Inspect Kernel Module
tools.description: Inspect one explicit local ELF32/ELF64 ET_REL Linux kernel module without executing it or opening a disassembler. Returns ordered .modinfo key/value entries (duplicates preserved), __versions symbol CRCs, presence of .gnu.linkonce.this_module and __ksymtab sections, observed .init.text and .exit.text sizes, and an appended module signature trailer with its module_signature fields plus a PKCS#7 byte range and SHA-256. Does not execute the module, decode struct module, or validate certificates. A missing section is observed absence when section names are known, not proof the module never carried that metadata. Other ELF types are not applicable. gzip, xz, and zstd containers are unsupported and name external_decompression as the next probe; neither this tool nor extract_artifact decodes those codecs, so decompress with an external utility and inspect the result. Reads a stable regular file; malformed ELF headers and exhausted entry budgets return no partial success. Portable on supported Node hosts.

tools.name: inspect_pe_load_config
tools.title: Inspect Pe Load Config
tools.description: Inspect PE32/PE32+ TLS callbacks and sized load configuration without executing the image. Returns callback VA/RVA/file offsets and sections, security cookie, SafeSEH (PE32), CFG flags and table pointers/counts, EH continuation and XFG fields. Flag-derived mitigation claims are labeled inferred. Absent directories are null; malformed structures and exhausted budgets fail without partial success. Reads a stable local regular file without a disassembler.

tools.title: Inspect Go Binary
tools.description: Inspect embedded Go compiler version, main module, dependency/replacement versions and build settings in an explicit local ELF, PE or thin Mach-O image, or the slice of a universal Mach-O named by architecture (read without lipo; artifact stays the universal file, selected_slice records the slice and source ranges stay file offsets).
