Explicit detail summary retains the same complete parent and returns compiler/main-module identity, counts, source ranges and parent_evidence_id. Query retained rows through inspect_analysis_view kind go, collection dependencies or settings; select exact dependency paths or setting keys, indices, fields and pagination. Rows always retain their original index scoped to the parent Evidence; empty filters select none. Runtime dependency completeness remains unknown. Supports inline and historical pointer encodings without installing Go, opening a disassembler, executing the target, writing temporary files or accessing the network. tools.name: inspect_rust_binary
tools.title: Inspect Rust Binary
tools.description: Inspect the cargo-auditable crate dependency list embedded in an explicit local ELF, PE or thin Mach-O image, or the slice of a universal Mach-O named by architecture (read without lipo; artifact stays the universal file, selected_slice records the slice and offsets stay file offsets). Returns the artifact SHA-256, the .dep-v0 section file offset and size, compressed and uncompressed sizes, format version, packages in their original order, the root package index, and dependency edges by index. Omitted or explicit complete detail preserves the full report. Optional detail summary retains that complete Evidence and returns source ranges, counts and parent_evidence_id. Optional view directly selects packages or edges in this call; it cannot be combined with explicit complete detail. Query the same retained facts with inspect_analysis_view kind rust: exact names/versions or package indices, edge from_indices/to_indices, fields and matching-row pagination. Row indices are original and scoped to the parent Evidence; empty filters select none. Default package fields omit dependency vectors; explicitly select dependencies for direct index references. String-pool entries are byte-pattern observations, not deserialized cluster semantics; typed class and function recovery needs an SDK-specific parser. Omitted or complete detail returns the full observation. Select detail: "summary" for target/ABI/library identity, all snapshot headers, coverage and original lower-bound counts without string lists. tools.name: close_binary
tools.title: Close Binary
tools.description: When the investigation is finished, drain earlier provider requests, optionally write a provider-neutral analysis snapshot atomically to the caller-supplied path, then close the active analysis session and every provider resource started for it. Resource-only app sessions have no binary snapshot binding, so close them without snapshot_path. Later provider requests wait until this lifecycle operation finishes. Existing files require explicit overwrite; a failed save leaves the session open so cached analysis is not lost. Metadata edits prevent immutable snapshot saves until the session is recreated; export_evidence_bundle preserves mutable observations before closing without a snapshot.

tools.name: capture_process_scenario
tools.title: Capture Process Scenario
tools.description: Run one caller-selected command under a PTY and return process capture Evidence with residual unknowns. The renderer admits at most 1,000,000 combined terminal cells, computed as columns × (rows + scrollback); every resize uses the selected scrollback and must fit the same budget. Supply a smaller terminal shape when that product is too large; dimensions are never clamped. This release has no runtime override for that cell budget. A command name resolves through the inherited PATH; the working directory defaults to the caller's current directory; host environment variables are inherited with scenario overrides. Environment keys cannot contain '=' or NUL, and REA_PROCESS_RUN_ID is reserved for process ownership. Filesystem snapshots are opt-in through filesystem_observation_paths. A positive finalization_ms makes a timeout or idle deadline send SIGTERM to the captured root through its start identity, keep observing, and send SIGKILL once after the interval; exit.finalization records each attempt with its delivery result and the observed exit, and cancellation still ends the run at once. The target runs with the current user's permissions; this is not a security sandbox.

Missing, journal-free, or truncated observations are never treated as equivalent.
